history.dynasty: Adi Shankaracharya (8th century, per belief); present structure by Maharaja Gulab Singh / Ranbir Singh (Dogra), 1835-1860; later Garhwal expansions
history.summary: One of the 108 Divya Desams (Tirukantamenum Kadi Nagar), glorified in the Divya Prabandha, the early-medieval Tamil canon of the Azhwar saints (6th-9th c.), and one of northern India's oldest Rama shrines. It stands above the Alaknanda-Bhagirathi confluence at Devprayag, where the Ganga begins. Legend: Rama performed penance here to atone for brahmahatya (killing Ravana, a Brahmin rakshasa); Brahma also did penance here, hence the name Prayaga; the Pandavas and Sage Bharadvaja are also said to have done penance here. The main shrine houses a black-granite standing image of Raghunathji - CONFLICT: templetravel.info says 15 ft tall, earthtrip.in says 6 ft (verify). Deula (conical-roof) stone architecture of huge uncemented blocks. Subsidiary shrines for Sita, Lakshmana, Hanuman, Badrinath, Adi Shankara, Annapurna and Garuda. Current structure begun 1835 by Maharaja Gulab Singh and completed 1860 under Ranbir Singh; damaged in the 1893 earthquake and rebuilt. Administered by the Uttarakhand Tourism Development Board. Identity confirmed: the famous Devprayag Raghunathji temple.

name: Raghunathji Temple
town_description: Devprayag is a pilgrimage town in Tehri Garhwal district, Uttarakhand, at the confluence of the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi rivers, where the Ganga begins. About 73 km from Rishikesh on the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway at ~618 m altitude, it is one of the Panch Prayag and a major penance (tapasya) centre in Hindu tradition.

travel.road: 73 km from Rishikesh on the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway; climb ancient stone alleyways from the Sangam ghats to the temple

visitor_information.best_time: October to May; avoid the monsoon months (landslide risk). Open through the year.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Summer 5:00 AM-12:00 PM and 5:00-9:00 PM; winter 6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00-8:00 PM (per templetravel.info; verify)
